data.narrative: Learner excelled in Module 02 by architecting a rigorous 9-task atomic decomposition for the Team Collaboration feature with strict size bounds (< 150 lines), diagnosing a subtle cross-task blueprint mismatch between storage and authorization, and engineering formal bidirectional interface contracts with deterministic acceptance criteria.

dimension_scores.observation: Constructed exhaustive prompt contracts specifying exact method signatures, schema fields, role constants, and 9 discrete acceptance criteria to ensure multi-agent reproducibility.
dimension_scores.evidence: Defined getTeamMembership(userId, teamId) -> Membership | null, addMembership, TEAM_ROLES enum, and explicit duplicate/null error handling rules in revised Task 1 prompt.

dimension_scores.observation: Conducted deep analysis of the agent's unspecified decision surface, identifying ambiguous return formats, lookup mechanisms, and state delta schemas before runtime failure.
dimension_scores.evidence: Identified that missing lookup specifications forced agent guessing; mandated null return semantics over exceptions for expected lookup misses.

dimension_scores.observation: Swiftly diagnosed the BREAK failure as decomposition incoherence rather than model hallucination, formulating the exact architectural placement fix in a single iteration.
dimension_scores.evidence: Recognized that Task 1 omitted memberships while Task 2 assumed they existed, resolving the gap by consolidating foundational data models in Task 1.

dimension_scores.observation: Demonstrated advanced architectural maturity by clearly separating decomposition (breaking down work) from interface contracting (guaranteeing inter-module compatibility).
dimension_scores.evidence: Decomposition divides a large feature into smaller pieces; interface contracting defines how those pieces communicate so one task’s output is predictable and compatible with the next task.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered a production-ready 9-task dependency tree and synchronized specifications adhering strictly to the < 150 line constraint and critical path sequence.
dimension_scores.evidence: Saved complete task tree with critical path mapping and full prompt contracts to progress/task-tree.md.

strengths: Mastery of bidirectional interface contracting, eliminating agent improvisation through exact function signatures and schema constraints
Clear analytical distinction between tool limitations and decomposition defects, focusing on root-cause structural fixes
growth_areas: Apply context engineering in Module 03 to curate exact file sets and token windows without overburdening the agent with unrelated files
data.recommendation: Advance to Module 03 (Context Engineering) to master the 30% Context Rule, file selection heuristics, and context compression techniques.

concepts_demonstrated: Atomic Task Principle (< 150 lines per task)
Dependency graphs and critical path analysis
Reproducibility and prompt determinism (Two Agents test)
Bidirectional contract specification (upstream vs downstream guarantees)

public_evidence.student_action: Architected a 9-task dependency tree, diagnosed a decomposition conflict between storage and RBAC, and engineered formal bidirectional interface contracts.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Produced progress/task-tree.md with 9 atomic subtasks (<150 LOC each), critical path mapping, TEAM_ROLES contracts, null-returning lookup semantics, and 9 verified acceptance criteria.
public_evidence.proof: Mapped Task 1 -> Task 2 contract with exact method signatures (getTeamMembership, addMembership), eliminated unspecified agent decisions, and updated progress/task-tree.md.
public_evidence.ability: Decomposes complex enterprise systems into atomic prompt units bound by explicit interface contracts
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Prevents catastrophic cross-task integration failures in multi-prompt AI development workflows by locking down data schemas and boundaries before execution.
